verdict.pair_reasons: X vs Y: both hit all 20 key items with no wrong claims, and both correctly refute the :963-966 comment (and the key's own trap) by showing all three floors share the rc 0|2 exemption at :780-784/:970/:1105. Y wins narrowly on verified material insights X lacks: the LANDING=1 conflict (wrap-ledger.sh:1985-1986 vs ship_floor reading only RUNG/TRUNK/AHEAD/SHAS), `set` keying on $PWD (:140) versus actuation on payload .cwd (:309-311), the wake floor being rung-blind, 🚀 attribution not being repo-scoped, and gate-stale no longer producing 🔧 (:1941-1961). X's one substantive bad cite (:424 for the ':197' claim) roughly offsets Y's two off-by-one cites in its stale-cite table. X vs Z: Z carries two verified wrong claims — that .count is reset only by `set` (refuted by :1206 rm -f on every unarmed Stop plus :253/:1229/:1247/:1260) and that 🔧 means 'dirty ∨ gate-stale ∨ remainder' per wrap-ledger.sh:25, a stale comment the code contradicts (no gate-stale 🔧; six other 🔧 sources) — the exact comment-trusting failure the brief warned against. X has none, so X wins. Y vs Z: same two Z defects; Y additionally identified the stale wrap-ledger:25 comment and the :1082-1083 phantom quote that Z repeated. Y wins.
